attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post. The parenthetical '(they won't)' is his assertion, not a quotation of anyone else.

semantics.note: '(they won't)' is an unqualified prediction that OpenAI and Broadcom will not build their ASIC in 2026, so it is a scored forecast. The proposition keeps the scope and the horizon. 'Build' is left undefined, as it is in the source.

contract.note: The contract flags correctly that 'build' could mean working samples or volume production. The support and contradiction conditions defer to the speaker's meaning, which he never stated. Working samples existed by June 2026, so the reading chosen would decide the result. No early-resolution rule is set.

evidence.note: OpenAI company disclosure dated 2026-06-24. It says engineering samples are running workloads in the lab and that deployment is still to come. It is relevant, but it is not independent. Under the 'working chips' reading it would cut against the forecast; under the 'volume' reading it would not. Because the deadline has not passed, it is context only.

output.rationale: The forecast runs to 2026-12-31 and the evaluation date is 2026-10-28, so it is not due. The contract has no early-resolution rule, so the June 2026 samples cannot count as a conclusive event. That evidence is also ambiguous: samples exist by OpenAI's own account, but volume production or deployment had not been reported. The result is unresolved pending the deadline and a settled reading of 'build'.
